svg.text: D. The refund flow: full refunds only, and everything it touches
The button is the easy part. The column on the right is the real work. Proposed 2026-08-15, not applied and not deployed.
1. Order history, then the order, then Refund. Confirm restates number and amount.
History shows ALL orders, unfiltered by time. No amount box: full refunds only.
The screen enforces nothing; it shows whatever the server answers.
2. Two rails, then the GATE. Only the third one is authorisation.
Rail: origin allow list. Only says the call came from our site, and the shop passes
it too. Cross-site protection, NOT identity.
Rail: rate limit, own "refund" bucket, 3 a minute. Tighter than any other function.
GATE: verify the signature, then RE-READ THE ROLE FROM app.demo_users. STAFF ONLY.
"admin" is the member portal login and is REFUSED. Hiding the button gates nothing.
3. PHASE ONE: decide, then write the intent. One transaction, order row LOCKED.
Four rules, all server side: really paid? not already refunded? none in flight?
placed within 24 hours? The screen checks NONE of these and is not meant to.
The amount is read from the ORDER ROW, never from the request. No caller can influence it.
Write the refund row as "requested", capture the clawback snapshot, and COMMIT.
The record exists BEFORE any money moves: a timeout then leaves a question we can
ask, instead of a refund we would repeat.
4. PHASE TWO: POST /refunds to HyperSwitch, which calls Braintree
payment_id, refund_id (ours, and HyperSwitch's own idempotency key), amount, reason.
amount = the full total_cents, which already contains the tax. The customer is made whole.
Braintree implements refund Execute and RSync in full, and partial amounts too.
There is NO per-connector refund gate. The 3DS trap does not repeat here.
failed
Order stays "succeeded".
Nothing left the business.
The slot is released, so a
genuine retry is possible.
pending / review
Order stays "succeeded":
nothing is back yet.
The next click settles it
with GET /refunds/{id}.
succeeded
Order becomes "refunded",
which is terminal.
The customer has every cent
back, tax included.
5. What is left behind, every time, whether the refund worked or not
app.demo_order_refunds: amount, the tax inside it, who asked, when, why, the processor's
reference, and a snapshot of which commission runs had already published this volume.
app.demo_staff_actions: the audit line, including every attempt that was REFUSED, which is
the record you most want when something has gone wrong.
The knock-ons. This column is the real work.
Reached only by a SUCCEEDED refund (red arrow below).
TAX: a known, measured gap. Not a silent one.
The customer gets the tax back. Stripe is not told.
By instruction, we do not reverse the Stripe Tax
transaction, so Stripe's reports will OVERSTATE tax
owed by exactly the tax on every refunded order.
Measure it: select * from app.v_demo_tax_drift;
Fix it later with POST /v1/tax/transactions/
create_reversal, mode=full. The backlog view already
lists every transaction id that needs one.
COMMISSIONS: clawbacks are out of scope. Evidence is not.
The bridge counts only orders whose status is
"succeeded", so moving to "refunded" has two effects
that cost no code at all:
Refund BEFORE the bridge runs: no volume is ever
created. Nothing to claw back. Self-healing.
Refund AFTER the bridge runs: the volume stands, and
upline may already have been paid on it.
So we snapshot, at refund time, which runs were already
final. That answer cannot be re-derived a month later.
INSTANT PAYOUT: this gives it a trigger, not a recovery.
Approved 2026-08-15 at 20 percent of order price, paid
to the sponsor, terminal there. Its own document says
the recovery path is unanswered and unbuilt.
This design supplies the EVENT and the EVIDENCE.
It does not supply the money back: there is still no
negative balance and no clawback engine.
GUARD RAILS: what an agent can never do
Choose an amount. Refund an order over 24 hours old.
Refund the same order twice. Refund without an explicit
confirmation the SERVER checks. Undo a refund.
Act without a verified staff token. Act unlogged.
Shaped for partial refunds, deliberately not built:
refunds are their own table, many rows per order are
already legal, amount is a real column, and the
"partially_refunded" state is already permitted by the
trigger. Adding partial later touches no table.
